title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: The Single Deductible on a CargoCare Claim
content:
Under a CargoCare cover of `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims`, each claim bears exactly one Deductible, taken off the loss basis.

## Definition

The Deductible taken is the higher of two amounts:

- the tier's general Deductible per claim; and
- the tier's Deductible for the claim's kind of loss, which is the wet damage Deductible for wet damage, the temperature damage Deductible for temperature damage, and nothing for every other kind of loss.

The two amounts are never both taken. The Deductible is subtracted from the loss basis, meaning the proven loss after the valuation uplift.

## Truth table by kind of loss

| Kind of loss on the claim | Amounts compared | Deductible taken |
|---|---|---|
| wet damage | general Deductible and wet damage Deductible | the higher of the two |
| temperature damage | general Deductible and temperature damage Deductible | the higher of the two |
| physical damage, contamination, shortage or total loss | general Deductible only | the general Deductible |

## Worked examples (hypothetical Deductibles, not those of any tier)

Assume a general Deductible of 300.00 and a wet damage Deductible of 200.00.

- A wet damage claim with a loss basis of 5000.00: the higher amount is 300.00, leaving 4700.00.
- A physical damage claim with the same loss basis: the general Deductible of 300.00 applies, again leaving 4700.00.

Assume instead a general Deductible of 150.00 and a temperature damage Deductible of 600.00. A temperature damage claim with a loss basis of 5000.00 bears 600.00, leaving 4400.00; the 150.00 is not taken as well.
